title: Create a straight stair between two levels with StairsEditScope
task: Add a stair between two levels: StairsEditScope.Start(baseLevelId, topLevelId) at top level, StairsRun.CreateStraightRun inside a Connector.WithTransaction block, then scope.Commit(IFailuresPreprocessor) between blocks; verify Stairs.GetStairsRuns and ActualRisersNumber.

pitfalls.symptom: scope.Commit throws InvalidOperationException 'EditScope cannot be closed' (script-target-must-not-be-modifiable) and the run reports success with no stairs in the model.
pitfalls.cause: Commit was called inside Connector.WithTransaction; the block's open transaction blocks closing the edit scope, and the connector's unwind discards the run.
pitfalls.fix: Commit at top level after the block (step 4); check Document.IsInEditMode() and the stairs' risers to confirm.

pitfalls.cause: Start needs the document not modifiable, or the two level ids are the same/inverted.
pitfalls.fix: Call Start at top level between blocks with base below top (step 2).

pitfalls.symptom: Commit is refused by a warning about the number of risers or run length.
pitfalls.cause: Revit posts stairs warnings at commit; without a preprocessor they abort the commit.
pitfalls.fix: Pass an IFailuresPreprocessor that deletes warnings (step 4), or size the run to the stair type's riser limits.
